subject: Turning drawings into manufactured components
hook: Six details that turn a drawing into a cutting list we can run first time.
ig:
Six details that turn a drawing into a cutting list we can run first time.

For joiners, kitchen fitters and shopfitters, the quickest jobs through any workshop are the ones that arrive complete. Here is what we look for:

1. Finished sizes for every part, and whether edging is included.
2. Board decor and thickness on every line.
3. Grain direction marked on woodgrain parts.
4. Which edges get ABS edging, and whether that is 0.4, 1 or 2 mm.
5. Drilling: hinge cups, shelf-pin rows, dowels.
6. A part reference on each line, so everything comes back labelled and easy to sort.

Miss one and the job pauses while someone asks. Include all six and it goes straight to the panel saw.

Our trade workshop in Hanley handles panel cutting, edge banding, drilling and cabinet assembly. Save this for your next order, and use the link in bio to ask for a priced cutting list.
fb:
For the trade lads and lasses who send us drawings: here is the checklist that gets your components made without a single back-and-forth email.

Finished sizes, board decor and thickness, grain direction on woodgrain parts, which edges get ABS (0.4, 1 or 2 mm), drilling positions, and a reference for every part.

It sounds obvious, but most delays come from one of those being missing. Get them on the list and the job goes straight onto the saw in our Hanley workshop.

Swipe for the detail on each, and if you have a job coming up, ask us for a priced cutting list:
